<!-- BIO (the approved prototype): an Experience pill, the H2 and a short
     introduction, then four career stories as white cards on the homepage's
     case-study card pattern. Two columns from 1024px, stacked below in this
     reading order. The cards neither lift nor carry a stretched link; the
     Revenue Assurance name is the one link. The role pills are labels, not
     buttons. -->

```{=html}
<section class="fx-bio fx-bio--stories" id="bio" aria-labelledby="bio-title">
  <div class="fx-bio__intro">
    <span class="fx-pill">Experience</span>
    <h2 id="bio-title">Bio</h2>
    <p>I have built teams, led programs and stayed hands-on with analysis. The throughline is understanding the decision, defining the numbers and making the system useful.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fx-bio__stories">
    <section class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-bio-story" aria-labelledby="story-atg">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">BI management</p>
      </div>
      <p class="fx-bio-story__employer">ATG Stores (Lowe's)</p>
      <h3 id="story-atg">Building the team</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">I proposed the BI function, hired its foundational team and managed six analysts and developers. When accounting needed a partner, I hired for accounting judgment as well as technical skill.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">Analysts took ownership of their stakeholder relationships.</p>
    </section>
    <section class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-bio-story" aria-labelledby="story-program">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">02</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Program leadership</p>
      </div>
      <p class="fx-bio-story__employer">Philips Healthcare</p>
      <h3 id="story-program">Setting shared priorities</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">Reorganizations brought competing analytics backlogs together. I made the tradeoffs visible: effort, expected results, sites served and cost. Stakeholders could challenge the assumptions, and unresolved priorities went to the sponsor.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">The result was one agreed queue for the work.</p>
    </section>
    <section class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-bio-story" aria-labelledby="story-analysis">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">03</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Hands-on analysis</p>
      </div>
      <p class="fx-bio-story__employer">Philips Healthcare</p>
      <h3 id="story-analysis">Questioning the headline number</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">When quality notifications spiked, I traced most to label misprints caught and corrected on the line. I challenged what the headline measure was telling leadership.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">Management accepted the recommendation to focus improvement work on failures with meaningful cost or risk.</p>
    </section>
    <section class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-bio-story" aria-labelledby="story-ai">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">04</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">AI Analytics Architect</p>
      </div>
      <p class="fx-bio-story__employer">Cascadia</p>
      <h3 id="story-ai">Directing AI with evidence</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">For <a href="projects/cascadia-revenue-assurance.html">Cascadia Revenue Assurance</a>, a portfolio build using synthetic data, I set the rules and expected answers before directing the AI build.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">Its published results are checked through two separately implemented calculations. Responsibility for what those numbers mean remains mine.</p>
    </section>
  </div>
</section>
```

<!-- THE TITLE, DEFINED (the approved prototype). The three moves keep
     their copy and order, each split between the card body and a separated
     takeaway; they still differ from the homepage's method tiles on purpose
     ("Direct the build", "Verify"). Three columns from 1024px, stacked
     below. Then the full-width shared-foundation card, in the inverted
     palette of the validation playbook's Commitment tile, with a
     domain-neutral example; then the closing paragraph, whose opening
     sentence is emphasized with a strong element and adds no heading. The
     section carries the concise ai-analytics-architect anchor; the H2 keeps
     the original long heading ID so existing links still land. -->

```{=html}
<section class="fx-inner fx-architect" id="ai-analytics-architect" aria-labelledby="an-ai-analytics-architect-owns-the-what-and-the-proof-not-the-how.">
  <div class="fx-architect__intro">
    <span class="fx-pill">The title, defined</span>
    <h2 id="an-ai-analytics-architect-owns-the-what-and-the-proof-not-the-how.">An AI Analytics Architect owns the what and the proof, not the how.</h2>
    <p>The job has three moves. None of them is writing the code.</p>
  </div>
  <ol class="fx-architect__moves">
    <li class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-architect__move">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Business rules</p>
      </div>
      <h3>Specify</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">Turn a business need into a precise spec: the data model, the measure definitions, the matching rules, and the invariants that must hold.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">Correct is defined before anything is built, so there is something to check the build against.</p>
    </li>
    <li class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-architect__move">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">02</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Delivery</p>
      </div>
      <h3>Direct the build</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">AI tools or an engineer do the building; either works. The job is to aim the build at the spec, not to pour the concrete.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">That leverage is why one person now covers ground that used to take a team.</p>
    </li>
    <li class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-architect__move">
      <div class="fx-about-card__top">
        <span class="fx-about-card__number" aria-hidden="true">03</span>
        <p class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Evidence</p>
      </div>
      <h3>Verify</h3>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">Nothing ships on trust. Every number is re-derived a second, independent way and reconciled against source, and a check that disagrees stops the publish.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__result">Trust what you can test.</p>
    </li>
  </ol>
  <section class="fx-card fx-about-card fx-architect__foundation" aria-labelledby="architect-shared-foundation">
    <div class="fx-architect__foundation-head">
      <span class="fx-pill fx-about-card__role">Shared foundation</span>
      <h3 id="architect-shared-foundation">See the system behind the requests</h3>
    </div>
    <div class="fx-architect__example">
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">Separate requests often point back to the same underlying system. A sales report, a service dashboard and a finance review may all describe the same customers, products, locations and dates.</p>
      <p class="fx-about-card__text">Define those shared building blocks once, including what each means and how records connect, and each report can use the same foundation.</p>
    </div>
    <p class="fx-about-card__result">The architectural work is recognizing that overlap, deciding what should be shared and where differences matter, then giving the build a structure that can be checked.</p>
  </section>
  <div class="fx-architect__close">
    <p><strong class="fx-architect__statement">I do not hand-write the code, and that is a choice.</strong> There are plenty of people who write code well. Specifying and verifying AI-built analytics inside a business domain is the rare skill, and it is the one this site is built to demonstrate.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```

<!-- SELECTED OUTCOMES (Felix §6.5 stat strip, dark variant for About; §3.1
     full-bleed band). Six tiles, three across from 1024, two from 640, one
     below. Each: a mono index, the figure and the headline as one heading,
     the existing bullet as the body with its bold lead sentence. The bodies
     are the About page's bullets verbatim; the figures and headlines are the
     approved draft's. The 200+ and $80K sentences are quoted by the homepage
     stat tiles and checked by tools/check_references.py. -->

```{=html}
<section class="fx-band" aria-labelledby="fx-outcomes-title">
  <div class="fx-band__inner">
    <h2 class="fx-band__title" id="fx-outcomes-title">Selected outcomes</h2>
    <ul class="fx-outcomes">
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">01</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">8</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">factories on one reporting system</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Built the Open Quality Notification reporting that eight factories ran on.</strong> I built the original myself, before there was a development team, sourcing from SAP directly so nothing was copied between workbooks. It scaled from one site to 8, cut about 32 hours a week of manual work, brought average closure time down 5 days, and reduced the notifications aging past 30 days by 20%. Refresh went from weekly by hand to hourly during business hours, on a cadence set by how the work actually runs rather than by how often we could run it.</p>
      </li>
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">02</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">12</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">KPIs, one definition each, three plants</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Gave three plants one set of numbers.</strong> The monthly operations report pulled from Murrysville, Böblingen and Shenzhen, each calculating the same 12 KPIs differently. I ran the initiative end to end, surfaced 6 definition misalignments and reconciled 4 of them myself, and delivered one automated Power BI report on aligned definitions. It removed about 36 hours of manual compilation a month and moved the reporting cycle from the 15th to the 5th.</p>
      </li>
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">03</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">200+</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">Critical Data Elements governed</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Governed data at enterprise scale.</strong> I standardized 200+ Critical Data Elements and common data model definitions across a global manufacturing platform, enforcing semantic consistency across systems that had none.</p>
      </li>
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">04</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">100+</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">hours a week of manual reporting removed</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Eliminated 100+ hours a week of manual reporting.</strong> I moved disconnected spreadsheets and point-in-time extracts into automated, governed dashboards.</p>
      </li>
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">05</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">$80K</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">a year out of the reporting estate</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Took $80K a year out of the reporting estate.</strong> I cataloged every pipeline under the Operations umbrella, traced each to the reports it fed, measured what people actually used, and retired the dead pipelines and over-frequent refreshes. No report was moved or deleted.</p>
      </li>
      <li class="fx-outcome">
        <p class="fx-outcome__index">06</p>
        <h3 class="fx-outcome__title"><span class="fx-outcome__figure">1</span><span class="fx-outcome__head">BI function, founded and staffed</span></h3>
        <p class="fx-outcome__text"><strong>Founded a BI function.</strong> I proposed the department at Lowe's/ATG Stores, hired its foundational team, and managed six analysts and developers through the build of the data warehouse, the KPI definitions and the stewardship model.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</section>
```
